The residence

Resort living, two minutes from the cliff

The apartment faces the landscaped gardens of the complex: 4.5 rooms plus a separate safe room on about 130 sqm, on floor 1 of 8, with three exposures, two parking spaces and a storage room.1,2 It is well kept, available for immediate entry, and the price is NIS 5,900,000.1

Migdalei Ne'eman is a complex of 330 apartments in seven buildings on Michael Ne'eman Street, next to Tzuk beach, occupied in stages between 2000 and 2015.3,4 Residents have a covered pool open all year, a spa with a sauna and a jacuzzi, a gym, lawns and a lobby guard 24 hours a day.3,4 The building facades carry mosaics by the artist Yaacov Agam.4

The complex fee covers the maintenance and the use of all the facilities, and was reported in 2024 at about NIS 2,300 a month for a 138 sqm apartment.3 The sea and Tzuk beach are about two minutes away on foot.2

The location

The northern edge of Tzukei Aviv, by Tzuk beach

The complex sits in northern Tzukei Aviv, the neighborhood between Unitzman Street, Namir Road, Propes Street and the sea.10 The management company places it next to Tzuk beach, and the street is filed under the Glilot area in some records.4,11

The coastal park promenade, about 2 km along the cliff, links Tzuk beach with Tel Baruch beach and opened in 2023.12 Nathan Alterman High School, whose building won the Rokach architecture prize, is in the neighborhood.13

Plan TA/3700 for a new north-west quarter covers the land around the complex, and the Ibn Gabirol extension has been paved to its east, where the Green Line light rail is also planned.3,14

Planning

What is planned nearby

Published plans and works, and what they may mean for a buyer or tenant. Based on published reports; not a substitute for a check with the planning authority.

  • The Ibn Gabirol extension and light rail east of the complex3

    According to Globes (2024), the new street paved on the complex's east side is expected to block the open view in that direction and become a main traffic artery, alongside light rail works. Check the unit's exact orientation during a viewing.

  • Plan TA/3700, the north-west quarter3,14

    11,000 to 13,000 homes, 1,500 hotel rooms and about 215,000 sqm of employment and retail on about 1,900 dunams between Sde Dov and the Herzliya boundary. Approved in 2015, it stalled in 2024 over reallocation tables; about 70% of the land is privately owned.

  • Residents' appeal over plan 370026

    Residents of the complex claimed about NIS 71 million for loss of value, and the district appeals committee ruled in January 2026 that no damage was proven.

  • Hotel and residential tower at Tzuk beach20,27

    A 14-floor tower with 116 apartments and a hotel of at least 198 rooms on about 16 to 20 dunams less than 100 m from the sea; the design plan was approved in May 2025.

  • Coastal park12,23

    First phase (promenade, bike path, landscape restoration and lighting) cost NIS 75 million and opened in 2023; further phases planned. Keeps the cliff front public and open.

Before you decide

The checks worth making

The questions a careful buyer asks about a unit in a complex like this, and the documents to obtain.

  • Which building and phase is No. 22, who built it and when was it occupied? Is the unit registered in the Land Registry as part of the condominium?
  • Is floor 1 above a pillar level or at garden level? Does the unit have a balcony or garden rights, and how private is it from the lawns and pool area?
  • What is the current monthly management fee for this unit, what does it cover (pool, spa, concierge, gym), and are any special levies planned?
  • What are the annual arnona and the registered and arnona areas, compared with the advertised 130 sqm?
  • Are the 2 parking spaces and the storage room registered or attached to the unit?
  • What condition are the kitchen, bathrooms and building systems in (the listing says well kept), and what renovation budget is realistic?
  • How will the Ibn Gabirol extension, the light rail and plan 3700 construction affect noise and views for this building and floor?
  • When is construction of the Tzuk beach hotel and tower expected to start?
  • Can the seller provide the nadlan.gov.il record of 2025-2026 deals in the complex, including the NIS 5.7 million and NIS 7.1 million sales of 130 sqm units?
  • Are the pool and spa hours, the 24/7 concierge and the gym operating as advertised today?
  • Which schools serve the address under municipal registration zones, and how far is the walk to Alterman High School and Nofei Yam Elementary?
  • A land registry extract and condominium plan, including the attached parking and storage
  • The management company budget and service list
  • Residents' meeting minutes from the last two years
  • Confirmations of no arrears on arnona and complex fees

Questions and answers

Questions worth asking

What is the price per sqm in the complex?
The asking price is about NIS 45,385 per sqm. Appraisers valued typical units in the complex at NIS 45,000 to 50,000 per sqm in 2024,3 and two 2026 sales of 130 sqm units on the street were recorded at NIS 43,846 and 54,615 per sqm.18
How much is the complex fee?
Globes reported about NIS 2,300 a month for a 138 sqm apartment in 2024, including maintenance and use of all facilities.3 For 130 sqm that is about NIS 2,170 a month if the fee scales with area; ask for the current amount.
How far is the sea?
About two minutes on foot to the sea and Tzuk beach.2 A rental listing by another advertiser in the complex says five minutes.17
How much purchase tax would a buyer pay?
Under the 2026 brackets: about NIS 190,538 for a single-home buyer, NIS 472,000 for an additional home or a foreign resident, and about NIS 19,606 for an eligible new immigrant.29,32
What will change around the complex?
The Ibn Gabirol extension has been paved to the east, with the Green Line planned along it; a design plan for a hotel and residential tower was approved at Tzuk beach; and the open land around the complex is part of plan TA/3700.3,14
